body.en: Exponential growth and logarithms appear in the Passport to Advanced Math domain and in data-interpretation contexts on the EST I.

Growth and decay

Exponential growth: \( A=A_0(1+r)^t \). Exponential decay: \( A=A_0(1-r)^t \). On EST I, these appear in word problems about populations, investments, or radioactive decay — identify \( A_0 \) (initial amount), \( r \) (rate), and \( t \) (time).

\(\log_b x = y \Leftrightarrow b^y = x\). Laws: \(\log(xy) = \log x + \log y\); \(\log(x/y) = \log x - \log y\); \(\log x^n = n\log x\). Exponential growth: \(A = A_0 e^{kt}\) (or \(A_0 b^t\)). Natural log: \(\ln(e^x) = x\); \(e^{\ln x} = x\).

label.en: Worked example — Solving an exponential equation

body.en:
A bacteria culture starts with 500 and doubles every 3 hours. How long until there are 4000?

\(4000 = 500 \cdot 2^{t/3} \Rightarrow 2^{t/3} = 8 = 2^3 \Rightarrow t/3 = 3 \Rightarrow t = 9\) hours.

label.en: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — Exponentials & Radicals

body.en:
• Negative Exponents vs. Negative Values: A negative exponent denotes reciprocal, not a negative quantity: \(x^{-n} = \frac{1}{x^n}\). For instance, \(3^{-2} = \frac{1}{9}\), NOT \(-9\) or \(-6\).
  • Fractional Exponent Definition: \(x^{m/n} = \sqrt[n]{x^m} = (\sqrt[n]{x})^m\). The denominator is the index of the radical root, and the numerator is the power: \(8^{2/3} = (\sqrt[3]{8})^2 = 2^2 = 4\).
  • Adding Exponents vs. Multiplying Powers: Remember that \(x^a \cdot x^b = x^{a+b}\), but \((x^a)^b = x^{ab}\). Do not confuse \(2^3 \cdot 2^4 = 2^7\) with \((2^3)^4 = 2^{12}\).
  • Extraneous Solutions in Radical Equations: Squaring both sides of an equation like \(\sqrt{2x + 3} = x\) can introduce extraneous roots. You MUST substitute candidate roots back into the original unsquared equation to verify validity.

solution.en:
Express with common base 2: Rewrite \(4 = 2^2\) and \(8 = 2^3\): \[ (2^2)^{x+1} = (2^3)^{2x-1} \implies 2^{2(x+1)} = 2^{3(2x-1)}. \]

Equate exponents: Since bases match: \[ 2x + 2 = 6x - 3 \implies 2 + 3 = 6x - 2x \implies 5 = 4x \implies x = \dfrac{5}{4} = 1.25. \]
